simple: The part of a program that runs on the CPU, and the part that runs on the GPU.
analogy: The pages of the recipe book the head chef cooks from, and the recipe cards sent to the hall of helpers.
precise: In a CUDA C++ source file, functions are compiled for the host, the device or both according to their execution-space specifiers; nvcc compiles the device part in a separate pass in which the macro __CUDA_ARCH__ is defined (this build's nvcc --dryrun listing shows a preprocessing step with and one without it).
source: D1, D3 of BR-01 (pending verification); R3 and R7 of BR-01 (runs in this build)

simple: A word in front of a function that says where the function may run.
analogy: A label on each recipe: chef only, hall only, or both.
precise: __host__ (runs on and is called from the host; the default for an unmarked function), __device__ (runs on the device, called from device code), __global__ (a kernel: runs on the device, launched from the host); __host__ __device__ compiles one function for both. In the CUDA 12.0 headers they are macros expanding to a compiler attribute. A kernel calling a host-only function is a compile error.
source: D1 of BR-01 (pending verification); H1 of BR-01 (crt/host_defines.h, read in this build); R9 of BR-01

simple: The program you run to build CUDA C++; it calls several other tools for you.
analogy: A translator who splits the recipe book, translates the hall's cards, hands the chef's pages to the chef's usual translator, and binds everything into one book.
precise: NVIDIA's CUDA compiler driver. For a .cu file (CUDA 12.0, as listed by nvcc --dryrun in this build) it runs the host preprocessor, cudafe++ (separates host and device code), a second preprocessing with __CUDA_ARCH__ defined, cicc (writes PTX), ptxas (writes a cubin), fatbinary, the host compiler, nvlink and the host linker.
source: D3 of BR-01 (pending verification); R7 and R16 of BR-01 (tool output in this build)

simple: An address in the GPU's memory, and an address in the CPU's memory; they look the same.
analogy: A shelf number in the hall's pantry and one in the chef's pantry; the note does not say which pantry.
precise: cudaMalloc returns a pointer to device memory for kernels to use; std::vector::data() returns a host pointer. Both have the same C++ type (for example float*), so passing one where the other is needed compiles without a diagnostic (shown in this build); what happens at run time depends on the system.
source: H1 of BR-01 (cuda_runtime_api.h, read in this build); R10 of BR-01; D1 of BR-01 for run-time behaviour (pending verification)

simple: The runtime's memory of the most recent thing that went wrong, which you must ask for.
analogy: A note pinned at the pass between the kitchen and the hall; nobody reads it to you.
precise: cudaGetLastError returns the last error produced by any runtime call in the same instance of the CUDA Runtime library in the host thread and resets it to cudaSuccess; cudaPeekAtLastError returns it without resetting. Because a kernel launch returns no value, its error is fetched this way.
source: H1 of BR-01 (cuda_runtime_api.h, read in this build)

simple: The same program, changed so that it runs somewhere new.
analogy: The same dish, rewritten for a different kitchen.
precise: A version of a program adapted to a new platform or programming model, whose behaviour is checked against the original; in BR-01, from host-only C++ to host plus device CUDA C++, checked after every step against the CPU result.
source: General engineering term; no source-specific claim (BR-01)
